subject: Numeric writes to Logic's track-header volume and pan sliders through the direct AX API
question: After the detent loop, do set_volume and set_pan reach the whole raw position nearest the request by one-raw AXValue writes, including a target next to a rail where the loop's last detent reversal was clamped?

reverify.command: python3 Scripts/livekit/live_973_header_mixer_fine_phase.py <worktree> <head> (with LPM_EVIDENCE_ROOT exported to a directory outside the worktree, and pyobjc-framework-Quartz installed)
reverify.expected: every check passes: each measured write is State A with reached_exact true and observed_raw equal to the whole raw position nearest the request; the rail cases take nine fine steps; volume and pan are written back to their starting values
reverify.cost: ~3 min after `swift build -c release --product LogicProMCP`; needs Logic in front with a disposable project, playback stopped, track 0's automation off, and nobody using the Mac

method: Release build of commit 3124824f driven by Scripts/livekit/live_973_header_mixer_fine_phase.py (committed unchanged as 8e099316) through the product's own path: logic_mixer set_volume and set_pan on track 0, addressed by target_ref, so findTrackHeaderVolumeFader / findTrackHeaderPanControl locate the slider and AXHelpers.setAttribute (AXUIElementSetAttributeValue) writes it, with no System Events. Disposable test project, track 0 an audio track named Lead Vocal; playback stopped and track 0's automation off as set up by the operator (the harness does not check either); UI language English. Two baseline writes recorded the starting values; then twenty whole raw targets, four fractional ones, and three rail cases (first set the start position, then request the fractional target beside the rail). Each target was converted to the public value with the same volume curve and pan mapping the product inverts. Every receipt was kept whole. The track-header rail was captured before the writes, after them and after the restore, and the run was screen-recorded; the PNG captures and the recording stay in the harness's evidence root outside the repository, and the receipts file carries the pixel checks' results. Volume and pan were then written back to their starting values. An earlier run on the same head without the captures read the same values; a second stopped on a harness bug after the fractional cases, and volume and pan were written back by hand before this run.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record measures the numeric effect of direct AXValue writes and their readback, not a string shipped in Logic's canonical data.

observations.what: measured writes (whole, fractional and rail cases), one row per call
all calls, including the two baselines and the three rail-start writes

conclusion: On this host, every measured write landed on the whole raw position nearest the request: 27 of 27 measured writes State A with reached_exact true (32 of 32 calls State A, counting the baselines and rail starts), for volume and pan in both directions and for fractional targets. Each rail case (volume 2 to 1.25, volume 231 to 231.75, pan 125 to 125.75) took 9 fine steps, one more than the previous bound of 8, so the one-detent bound is exercised on real Logic and not only in the test fake. The pixel captures agree: the header changed during the writes and matched its first capture after the restore.
limits: One host: Logic 12.3.1 build 6682, macOS 26.6.2, UI language en-US, one project, one audio track. Other builds, including 12.3/6674, are not measured here, and it is not known whether one-raw movement first appeared in 12.3.1.
The other nine declared UI locales were not run. Nothing here depends on a label, but the slider lookup does, and it is not live-verified in those languages by this record.

observed_raw is the product reading its own slider; System Events cannot address the Track Headers list. The pixel comparison is the only independent witness, and it shows that the rail changed, not the raw value.
No write moved a slider away from its target in this run, so the State B path for that case is covered only by the unit fixture with a hypothetical ten-raw write.
fine_steps counts accepted AXValue write calls; this run does not separate an accepted write that did not move from one that did, beyond the readback after each.
